Role permissions

Non-interactive reference. Try switching "Signed in as" on screen 1 to see these outcomes live.

ActionHRManagerTeam memberSatisfies
Create hire profileAllowedAllowedRejectedAC1, AC2
Edit hire profileAllowedAllowedRejected — profile unchangedAC4, AC5
Deactivate profileAllowedAllowedRejectedAC6, AC7
Reactivate profileAllowedAllowedRejectedAC6, AC8

A rejected request never opens the create/edit form, never changes a profile's status, and never starts or cancels a run — the rejection happens at the point the action is attempted, same as the underlying API returning a 403.

Acceptance criteria checklist

Every acceptance criterion for this story, mapped to where it's demonstrated.

1

Create rejected without HR/Manager role — AC1

Switch "Signed in as" to Team member and click "+ New hire profile": a permission-denied notice appears in place of the form and no row is added.

2

Create succeeds with all six fields — AC2

As HR or Manager, filling in name, email, phone, department, role, and start date and clicking "Create profile" saves immediately and the new row appears in the table.

3

Missing a required field blocks the save with a named error — AC3

Submitting with any of the six fields blank shows an inline error naming that exact field; nothing is saved — see "Required-field validation".

4

Edit persists updated field values — AC4

"Edit" on any row reopens the same form pre-filled; changing any field and saving updates the row in place.

5

Edit rejected without HR/Manager role; profile unchanged — AC5

As Team member, "Edit" on any row shows the same permission-denied notice and the row's values never change.

6

Deactivate/reactivate rejected without HR/Manager role — AC6

As Team member, "Deactivate" and "Reactivate" both show a "Request rejected" toast and never open the confirm dialog — see "Role permissions".

7

Deactivating a profile with an active run cancels it — AC7

As HR or Manager, "Deactivate" on Jordan Reyes's row names the active run in the confirm dialog; confirming cancels it — see "Deactivate & reactivate lifecycle".

8

Reactivating starts a new run — AC8

As HR or Manager, "Reactivate" on Sam Okafor's row confirms starting a brand-new run from step 1; confirming creates it immediately.

9

Only deactivation is available — no permanent delete — AC9

No row, menu, or screen anywhere in this prototype offers a delete action — only "Deactivate" / "Reactivate".
